findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10m to 1m without explanation
findings.body: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 changes time.NewTicker(time.Minute*10) to time.NewTicker(time.Minute*1). The PR description only discusses splitting annotation cleanup queries to avoid MySQL deadlocks. Running every cleanup job (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) 10x more often massively increases DB and IO load and is unrelated to the fix. Revert to 10 minutes or justify separately.

findings.title: Debug logging left at Error level in cleanup path
findings.body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go lines 534,537,554,557,576,579 call r.log.Error for routine operation (e.g. "Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned annotations by time", "Tags to clean") with err==nil and including full id lists and cond on every batch. Every successful cleanup run will emit Error-level logs, triggering false alerts and log spam and potentially logging thousands of IDs. These should be Debug (or removed).

findings.title: Split fetch/delete loop can stop early on concurrent deletes
findings.body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:656 in untilDoneOrCancelled stops when affected==0. With the old single-statement DELETE, zero affected meant no more rows matched. With the new split SELECT ids then DELETE BY ids, affected==0 no longer implies done: the fetched IDs may have been concurrently deleted while unfetched deletable rows remain. The loop then exits prematurely and leaves work for the next cycle. Termination should be based on empty fetch (len(ids)==0), not RowsAffected.

findings.title: Quadratic string building for large SQLite IN list
findings.body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:609-612 builds the SQLite IN list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop. With batch sizes up to 32767 (covered by the new test) this is O(n^2) copying. Since IDs are int64 from the DB, use strings.Builder with strconv.AppendInt to build the list in linear time.
